name: Samoa
snapshot: A proud Polynesian nation where La'auli Leuatea Schmidt's FAST party won a snap election in 2025 after splitting from the former prime minister.
culture: Fa'a Samoa, the Samoan way, centres on the aiga, extended family, and matai, chiefs who hold family titles and land. Traditional tattoos, pe'a for men and malu for women, are a rite of passage. Church and choir singing are central on Sunday. Rugby players of Samoan heritage star around the world.
society: Remittances from Samoans in New Zealand, Australia and the US are a large share of the economy. Only matai could stand for parliament until reforms, and they still dominate. A 2021 constitutional crisis saw the outgoing prime minister refuse to leave until courts intervened.
situation: La'auli Leuatea Schmidt, who split from Prime Minister Fiamē Naomi Mata'afa, led FAST to victory in an August 2025 snap election and became prime minister.
power: A parliamentary democracy. The prime minister leads the majority in the Legislative Assembly, where almost all candidates must hold a matai chiefly title; parliament elects the head of state for five years.

leaders.state: Head of State Tuimalealiʻifano Vaʻaletoʻa Sualauvi II
leaders.gov: Prime Minister La'auli Leuatea Schmidt, since 2025

eat: Oka, raw fish in coconut cream
Palusami, taro leaves baked in coconut cream
argue: Political splits in the ruling party

story: Germany ruled Western Samoa from 1900; New Zealand took over in 1914, and the Mau movement resisted its rule. Samoa became the first Pacific island country to win independence, in 1962.
timeline: Black Saturday: police fire on Mau protesters
Constitutional crisis brings Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa to power
